Hi team,

Thanks for the demo last week — GlobeHealth is interested in a retention and regional storage model we can point to in our internal security review. Two immediate asks:

- Can Redwood provide a playbook that documents how a tenant can require data residency by region (US-only), configurable retention per-tenant (30/90/365 days), and proof-of-deletion for audits?
- We need clarity on how legal holds interact with automated deletion (e.g., if a tenant toggles hold, does the system override TTLs across backups/caches?).

Attached is a brief from our security team (residency_requirements_globehealth.pdf). High level timeline: we need an internal compliance decision by Dec 20. Please let me know what you need from our side and recommended next steps.

Sanjay — thanks for the brief and timeline. We're happy to put together a concise ops playbook. Quick clarifying questions so we scope the right artifacts:

1) Residency model: do you need per-tenant hard-binding to a single physical region (no cross-region replication), or is geo-fenced logical residency (data stored in US regions but replica allowed across US zones) acceptable?
2) Retention ranges: you listed 30/90/365 — do you expect per-object TTLs (customer can set different TTLs per dataset) or a single tenant-level policy?
3) Proof-of-deletion: is a signed receipt enough, or do you require a cryptographic audit trail / chain-of-custody report?

I'll loop in Karthik to outline the technical constraints. If this looks urgent we can do a 30-min sync tomorrow.

Cheers,

On Tue, Dec 1, 2026 at 05:05 PM Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Priyom asked a few good scope questions — adding technical constraints and options.

High-level options we can document in the playbook (advantages/tradeoffs):

A) Tenant hard-bind to region (recommended for strict sovereignty):
  - Data physically stored in a single region (e.g., us-west-2). No cross-region replication for primary store.
  - Backups: can be configured to stay in-region but current snapshot tooling replicates to our secondary region for disaster recovery; changing that requires workflow & compliance signoff.
  - Pros: easiest to justify to auditors; Cons: higher operational risk for region-level DR.

B) US-only logical residency (preferred for most customers):
  - Primary + replicas limited to set of US regions (us-west-2, us-east-1). Cross-region read replicas allowed.
  - Easier for availability and scaling.

Retention & deletion:
- Tenant-level TTL policy is straightforward (30/90/365). Per-object TTLs are supported by our API but add complexity to billing and indexing — include as advanced option.
- Deletion pipeline: deletion events need to propagate to runtime caches, KV caches, S3-like object store, and snapshot pruning jobs. We currently have a deletion queue and a background verifier; proof-of-deletion can be implemented by recording deletion-event hashes in the audit log and generating a signed confirmation.
- Legal hold: when a legal hold is active we mark all objects as exempt from TTL expiration; holds also pause background snapshot pruning and GC. Holds must be surfaced to backup retention workflows; that is a manual gating step for now (we will note as limitation).

Risks / open items for the playbook:
- Backup/DR replication model: confirm GlobeHealth legal position on secondary-region backups (we can omit cross-region replication but need SRE/ops process changes).
- Snapshot retention & immutable backups: how long do you need snapshots retained beyond tenant TTLs if legal hold applied?
- KMS: customer-managed keys (BYOK) needed for some audits — we support KMS integrations but need to document key lifecycle.

I attached an architecture sketch that maps where deletion hooks need to be implemented (redwood-tenant-geo-arch.png). I'll open INF-4821 to track the engineering RFC.

-karthik

Sanjay — quick commercial note so we align expectations:

- The default hosted plan covers logical US-only residency with standard retention controls.
- Tenant hard-binding to a single region and removing cross-region backups typically maps to our Dedicated/Private offerings (there is an implementation lead time and a recurring premium).
- Proof-of-deletion audits (signed receipts + signed audit export) are part of our compliance add-on (one-time setup + monthly retention fee).

If GlobeHealth prefers a Dedicated engagement, I can turn this into a proposal (SOW + timeline). Otherwise we can scope an in-hosted playbook that documents current behavior and required customer attestations.

Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Sanjay — thanks everyone for the fast responses. Summary and next steps: 

- Scope: prepare a "Residency & Deletion Ops Playbook" that documents both the Hosted (US-only logical residency) and Dedicated (hard-region bind) options, retention configuration (tenant-level TTLs + advanced per-object TTLs), and the current legal-hold behavior (holds pause TTL-based pruning and snapshot pruning is manual).
- Deliverables: 1) One-page decision guide for your security team, 2) Ops playbook (3–5 pages) with architecture notes and caveats, 3) Template audit export and signed proof-of-deletion example.
- Constraints: Snapshot/DR cross-region behavior is an open item — we will document current default behavior and list steps to disable cross-region backups (SRE/ops change ticket required).
- Timeline: draft decision guide + one-pager by 2026-12-15; full playbook and audit template by 2026-12-22.
- Action items: Karthik will create RFC INF-4821 to capture engineering work for deletion propagation and proof-of-deletion. Marissa to confirm commercial preference (Hosted vs Dedicated). Sanjay to confirm whether cross-region backups must be disallowed or just limited to US regions.

Can we schedule a 30-min call next week (Dec 14–16) to review the one-pager? I'm available Dec 15 09:00–11:00 PST.

Thanks,
